name: EMS Ltd
title: EMS Ltd - 543983 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: EMS Ltd guides Q3 and Q4 FY27 revenue up 30-35% each over Q2, with total order book about ₹3,153 crore excluding GST.
summary.overview: The transcript is a poor-quality automated rendering, and key figures are garbled, so treat numbers as indicative only. Management said Q2 revenue rose about 23.3% YoY on a consolidated basis, while H1 FY27 operating revenue fell, which management attributed to a 2-3 month work stoppage in Q2-Q3 FY26 and a stoppage in FY27 for sedition/safety reasons. Management said it secured about ₹900 crore of new orders in the quarter (L1 or LOA stage) and expects to bid around ₹3,000 crore next quarter. Management said the standalone entity showed operating income and PAT growth of roughly 30% and 50%, with consolidated numbers diluted by a loss-making subsidiary. Receivables from UP and Uttarakhand government schemes (AMRUT/Namami Gange) were described as delayed, with Uttarakhand's portal change cited as a cause.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue growth, Q2 FY27 YoY
financial_highlights.change: as stated by analyst on call; not independently verified

financial_highlights.metric: Total order book as on 30 Sep 2026 (excl. GST)
Water and wastewater orders in book
Net order inflow in Q2 FY27

financial_highlights.value: Rose in Q2; management called it project-based (soil exploration, consultancy, engineering)

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone operating income and PAT growth

segments.name: Water and wastewater (EPC)
segments.commentary: ₹2,171 crore of the ₹3,153 crore order book; water supply and sewage treatment are the core business. Typical projects take 2-2.5 years to complete, with 6-8 months from L1 to revenue start.

segments.name: Electricity / T&D
segments.commentary: ₹66.06 crore in order book. Small relative to water.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Management said ₹191 crore of O&M is in progress and ₹342 crore will start after a scheme is over; figures were stated in the opening remarks and may be garbled.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 FY27 revenue 30-35% above Q2 FY27, and Q4 FY27 also 30-35% above Q2 FY27.
Management aims to match FY25 revenue by year-end FY27; FY26 was lower due to work stoppages.
Management cited about 20% annual revenue and PAT growth, consistent with its record since 2013, over the next 2-3 years.
Management said EBITDA margin could rise, with historical EBITDA around 28-29% and PAT above 20%, but competition is increasing.
Management said it is bidding aggressively for about ₹3,000 crore of new work next quarter.
Management said the 30-35% growth target is on a standalone basis; consolidated numbers are diluted by a loss-making subsidiary (EMS Industries).
capex_capacity: Management said EMS is not making its own capex and is working only on government-funded capex.
Management said manpower of about 480 is fixed; the company will retain staff unless it foresees no future work.
Management said the company is bidding in new states (e.g., Karnataka) and is selective, targeting better margins and less competition.
demand_pricing: Central government funds (AMRUT, Namami Gange) now require matching state and ULB shares, which delays payments.
UP receivables (about ₹450 crore cited by analyst) were described as delayed; management said UP has normalized, while Uttarakhand changed its portal and is still streamlining.
Projects take about 6-8 months from L1 to start revenue; around 90% of revenue is recognized within two years and the rest within about 2.5 years, with detention monies possible.
Competition is rising in water EPC bids, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How are collections from UP government projects, and what is the overdue exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UP had normalized; Uttarakhand delays stem from a portal change. Central funds now require state and municipal matching shares. The overdue amount figures were not clearly stated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book split and how much is at L1 or LOA stage?
qa_highlights.answer: Total order book is ₹3,153 crore excl. GST, of which about ₹2,600 crore excl. O&M. Around ₹900 crore is at L1 or LOA stage, with DPR preparation of 5-6 months before execution.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 FY27 operating revenue decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a 2-3 month work stoppage due to sedition/safety concerns, plus client and funding-agency approval delays for engineering changes, which hit Q2 and Q3 of the prior year. Management said revenue has since ramped up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise, and are margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses rose on project-based costs (soil exploration, consultancy, engineering) for the ₹900 crore of new orders, and called it non-recurring. It said standalone PAT growth (about 50%) outpaced fixed-cost growth (about 30%).

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is expected by year-end and how confident is management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 and Q4 each 30-35% above Q2 and aims to match FY25 revenue. It cited a 20% CAGR track record since 2013.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pledge position and plan to reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: The analyst said promoter pledge is about 30% and asked whether it could fall to about 25% by Q4. Management said it had withdrawn and repaid part of the pledge and aimed to reduce it around year-end; the exact figure was unclear.

risks_watch: Delayed government receivables (UP, Uttarakhand, AMRUT/Namami Gange) and rising working capital needs.
Q2 other expenses rose; management said they are project-related, but they may persist while new projects are at engineering stage.
Consolidated results are diluted by a loss-making subsidiary (EMS Industries), so standalone and consolidated growth diverge.
Monsoon and work stoppages (sedition/safety, client approvals) have hit execution timing before.
Q3 and Q4 targets rely on converting ₹900 crore of L1/LOA orders, and bidding success for ~₹3,000 crore next quarter.
Promoter pledge reduction (about 30% to about 25%) is targeted by year-end.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and forward-looking about growth targets (30-35% QoQ) and order inflows, but gave vague answers on receivables and the consolidated gap. Explanations for the H1 decline and the other-expense rise were detailed but partly unclear in the transcript.
key_quotes: We can expect 20% annual growth as our history says we have achieved it from 2013 continuously
We are not making our own capex and the means for any capex.

growth.why: Management guides Q3 and Q4 FY27 revenue 30-35% above Q2 and FY27 revenue to match FY25, backed by a ₹3,153 crore order book (about ₹2,600 crore excl. O&M) and ~₹900 crore of Q2 wins, but no new capacity is being added (only government-funded capex) and the brief's figures are flagged as garbled, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said EBITDA margin could rise from current levels with historical EBITDA around 28-29% and PAT above 20%, but flagged rising competition and Q2 other expenses that it called non-recurring; no quantified margin guide was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management said EMS is not making its own capex, is working only on government-funded capex, and manpower of about 480 is fixed, so no new owned capacity is planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides Q3 and Q4 FY27 revenue 30-35% above Q2 each, and FY27 revenue to match FY25, backed by a ₹3,153 crore order book (about ₹2,600 crore excl. O&M) and about ₹900 crore of L1/LOA wins in Q2, though the figures are flagged as garbled.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is working only on government-funded capex and not making its own; no utilisation figure was given, so there is no trigger for a company-funded capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is bidding for about ₹3,000 crore of new work next quarter and has a record of about 20% annual revenue and PAT growth since 2013, but the Q3/Q4 guide already assumes strong conversion and the upside depends on winning bids in a more competitive market.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 and Q4 targets rely on converting ~₹900 crore of L1/LOA orders, UP and Uttarakhand receivables are delayed, and work stoppages have hit execution before, with the 2-3 month stoppage in H1 FY27 cited as the reason revenue declined YoY.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New products, brands or models were not discussed on the call.

rows.label: Delayed government receivables (UP, Uttarakhand)
rows.why: UP receivables of about ₹450 crore were cited as delayed, Uttarakhand changed its portal, and central funds now need matching state and ULB shares, so payment delays and working capital needs are likely to persist.

rows.label: Bidding in new states such as Karnataka
rows.why: Management said it is bidding in new states, e.g. Karnataka, while being selective for better margins and less competition, but no order count or value was given.

rows.label: Promoter pledge cut from ~30% to ~25%
rows.why: Management said it has already withdrawn and repaid part of the pledge and aims to reduce it around year-end, but the exact figure was unclear on the call.

tone.note: Management was confident on 30-35% QoQ growth targets and ₹900 crore of Q2 order inflows, but was vague on receivables, the subsidiary drag and the other-expense rise; analysts pressed on overdue amounts and the pledge.
